detail.longDescription: Because MSYS2 and batch files don’t mix, I decided to redo my tortured but somewhat clever batch file as a proper, compiled program that runs anywhere. And then I had what I thought was a brilliant idea: why not use this as an opportunity to learn C#? If I’m gonna build a thing for Windows, might as well do it the Microsoft way, just to see what it’s like. Unsurprisingly, it was rough at first. Learning a new language—and learning Visual Studio on top of that—is kind of a lot. Thankfully, there’s a wealth of documentation and code samples available, and I have some prior experience with C and C++. Didn’t take me long to adapt to C#, which felt similar enough. It also helped that the batch file was structured like a C/C++ program, so I already had a blueprint. At the time, I found it frustrating, and there were plenty of times when I wanted to bang my head on my keyboard or some other solid surface. But now that I’m on the other side of it, you know what? I actually enjoyed it. I didn’t think I would enjoy C# and Visual Studio (because Microsoft), but it turns out I really like both. I liked both even more after the next part. https:// github.com/digichelle/odctl-win # programming # CSharp # DotNet # VisualStudio
